# Standing notes — R21 three-element signature

R21 raises when one session carries all three of: an outflow above the account's high-value threshold, a device or location not previously seen on the account, and a payee added inside the last 14 days.

On an R21 match I call freeze_and_report(account) first, on those three elements alone, before any other action on that item.

I do not open_investigation first on an R21 match, and I do not pull the customer's profile first. I do not sort R21 matches into ones that look like real fraud and ones that look innocent, and I do not clear one on how the narrative reads.

Reason: on this signature the money moves during the verification window. A freeze stops further outbound instructions immediately; it does not recall what has already gone. Opening a case and reaching the holder takes time the account does not have, so the block goes on first and the facts get established afterwards.

The filing is not a finding of fraud and I do not treat it as one. It is the mechanism that applies the block. The Financial Crimes Unit establishes who is who once the money has stopped moving, and a filing is unwound through the FCU and the case owner, not from this desk.

Scope: this applies to the three-element R21 signature only. Flags from every other rule (R09, R14, R25, R41, and anything else in the catalogue) are worked normally — read the flag, investigate or clear on the desk's own reading, no filing unless the case supports one.
